text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime minister Andris Shkele accepted the resignation of state minister of health care Juris Vinkelis, who is alleged to have violated anti-corruption laws by holding a post in a private company while serving as a minister.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele will not ask for the resignation of deputy prime minister Juris Kaksitis, who is also alleged to have violated anti-corruption laws.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele will be on leave from June 30 till July 17. Some sources said he is going to Great Britain to improve his English.

- U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of state Ronald Asmus announced U.S. plans to sign a so-called Baltic charter this fall. Today Asmus will meet Shkele and Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs to discuss the implementation of the Baltic Action Plan and the draft of the charter.
- The third congress of Latvian doctors opened in Riga assembling more than 3,000 participants.

- President Guntis Ulmanis is on an unofficial visit to Estonia to participate in negotiations between Latvia's Farmers Union and the Estonian Rural People's Party to sign a cooperation agreement. Ulmanis is honorary chairman of Latvia's Farmers Union.
- The Russian Central bank prolonged the license of Parekss Bank's rep office in Moscow. The bank plans to carry out investment projects in Moscow and some regions in Russia.
- Privatisation agency head Janis Naglis announced plans to set the nominal capital of Ventspils Nafta at 170 million lats.
- A visa-free agreement between Latvia and Norway will be signed on July 2.
- In the first five months of 1997 budget revenues were 588.906 million lats and expenditures were 550.761 million lats.
